five_second.sells: online art/drawing courses and a spiritual, meditative creative membership
five_second.for_whom: adults looking for a calming, meaningful creative hobby and community

errand.abandoned_at: checkout page for the Neuro Arts Membership monthly plan, after typing my email but before entering any card details
errand.abandon_trigger: an undisclosed 3-day trial with a full credit-card form appearing only at checkout, stacked on top of never finding the class day/time and a wall of legal terms right before the pay button

features_used.moment: Tapping this from the homepage took me straight to the Neuro Arts Membership page, which is exactly what I was looking for.

features_used.feature: membership page pricing boxes (monthly vs annual)
features_used.moment: I found $38/month and $375/year with a badge saying 'Get 3 Months free,' but when I did the math myself ($38 x 12 = $456, minus $375) it only came out to about 2 months saved, not 3.

I had to scroll through testimonials, seasonal theme examples, and an About Anna section for a very long time before reaching the actual pricing, and I never found what day or time the live class happens.
Tapping the $38 price sent me straight to a checkout with a '3-day trial' badge and a full credit card form, something I was never told about anywhere on the membership page.
I typed my email into the checkout box and it accepted it without any trouble.

features_used.feature: terms and conditions text at checkout
features_used.moment: Right before the payment button there was a long wall of legal text to agree to, which made me feel unsure exactly what I would be signing up for.

features_looked_for_but_missing: a clear day and time for the weekly live class
an upfront note on the membership page that joining starts a paid trial requiring a card
a simple side-by-side chart showing exactly how much money the annual plan saves
feature_that_most_helped_the_decision: the clearly labeled Pay Monthly / Annual Plan price boxes near the bottom of the membership page, which at least gave me numbers to work with
feature_that_most_hurt_the_decision: the surprise 3-day trial and credit card form appearing only at checkout with no earlier warning

friction.moment: Never found what day or time the weekly live class actually happens, despite reading the entire membership page top to bottom.
Annual plan advertised as 'Get 3 Months free' but my own math only worked out to about 2 months of real savings.
Checkout revealed an undisclosed 3-day trial requiring a credit card, never mentioned on the membership page itself.
The membership page is extremely long, needing well over a dozen scrolls on my phone just to reach the price and buy buttons.
A long wall of legal terms and conditions text sits right before the payment button.

delight.moment: Anna's personal 'I'm Anna' bio and photos made her feel like a real, warm person running this, not a faceless company.
Several detailed, named testimonials from members in different countries made the weekly community feel genuine.

what_earned_it: a real named founder (Anna) with photos and a personal bio
multiple detailed testimonials with names and countries
clearly displayed price boxes with two currency options
trust.what_it_would_take: tell me up front on the membership page that there is a 3-day trial before any charge, state plainly which day and time the live class meets, and make the annual savings math actually match what the badge claims

brand_recall.tell_a_friend_one_sentence: It's a sweet, artsy weekly drawing group run by one woman named Anna, but the site never told me what day the class is on and then sprang a free trial and a credit card form on me at checkout, so I didn't sign up.
